summary: Tested user-friendly Italian error messages on the Populus auth screen (login/signup/anonymous) via Playwright at http://localhost:3000/auth. All 8 required scenarios passed (100%): the UI shows clean Italian sentences and never leaks raw Pydantic/HTTP artifacts (no 'HTTP', '422', 'loc', '[{', 'value_error', or JSON). Client-side validation fires immediately for empty/invalid inputs, and backend-originated errors (401 -> 'Credenziali non valide.', 400 -> 'Email gia registrata.') are surfaced correctly through ApiError.detail. Screenshots saved under /tmp/populus_err/*.png.
critical_code_review_comments: api.ts friendlyValidation() is well-structured; covers email/password/nickname/age/region/favorite_categories with graceful fallback. No leaks observed.
auth.tsx client-side validation short-circuits before any network call, giving instant feedback. Good separation of client vs. server error paths.
seed_data_creation: Created one throwaway email user (dup{ts}@t.com) to verify duplicate-email flow; user completed signup, then a second signup attempt with the same email triggered the 400 'Email gia registrata.'
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth error UX is verified end-to-end. If future changes touch /app/frontend/src/api.ts (request/friendlyValidation) or /app/frontend/app/auth.tsx (handle()), rerun the same 8 scenarios; selectors used: [data-testid="auth-tab-email"|auth-tab-anon|auth-mode-login|auth-mode-signup|auth-email-input|auth-password-input|auth-nickname-input|auth-anon-nickname-input|auth-submit-button|auth-error].
rca_of_issue: Original bug: FastAPI 422 Pydantic errors were rendered as raw JSON payload (`[{"loc":[...],"msg":...}]`) because the frontend simply stringified error.detail. Fix (already applied by E1): (a) friendlyValidation() maps each Pydantic item to an Italian, field-specific sentence and joins multi-field errors with '\n'; (b) explicit branches for 401/403/404/409/429/500 and fetch-fail; (c) client-side pre-checks in auth.tsx cover empty/short values so most cases never hit the network. Verified: none of the 8 attempts surface any raw code or English framework text.
